subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Rivera <alice.rivera@finco.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — next steps

Hi Alice,

Great to speak earlier — thanks for walking us through FinCo's performance targets and production profile. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can put together a validated Dedicated capacity recommendation.

Recap of FinCo SLOs discussed:
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 200ms for typical prompts (~150 tokens); p50 target <= 80ms
- Throughput: sustained 120 requests/sec (avg ~150 tokens per request), burstable to 250 rps for short windows
- Concurrency: up to 64 concurrent active streams (many customers will use streaming responses)
- Streaming: server-sent events / HTTP streaming required; first token latency (time-to-first-byte) should be <100ms for interactive flows
- Model: expecting to serve an Llama 2.1 13B-equivalent optimized model (quantized fp16/int8 variants under evaluation)

Immediate ask / next steps:
1) We'll run a dedicated capacity performance validation comparing A100 vs H100 profiles and provide a sizing recommendation (nodes, reserved throughput).
2) Please confirm anticipated steady-state request distribution (tokens per request and qps pattern) and any hard blackout windows for testing.
3) We'll share a validation plan and proposed schedule by EOD tomorrow.

Planned validation highlights (high level):
- Latency sweeps at different sequence lengths (128/256/512 tokens)
- Concurrency ramp (1 -> 64 concurrent streams) with streaming enabled
- Sustained throughput run (4 hours) to validate thermal/e2e stability and KV cache behavior
- Cold-start / warm-cache comparisons and warmup guidance
- GPU comparison: A100 40GB vs H100 80GB at same config; estimate nodes required to meet SLOs

I'll loop in our performance engineering team if you have any constraints on test windows. Attaching a one-page outline after we finalize the test matrix.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
[Attachment: dedicated_capacity_validation_plan.pdf (pdf)]

Thanks Marissa — that recap is helpful. A few clarifications from our side before you start tests:

- Tokens per request: most calls are short (median ~120 tokens) but ~20% of calls hit 400-600 tokens (batch reporting).
- Peak pattern: steady-state ~120 rps during business hours, with 5-10 minute bursts up to 250 rps a few times per day.
- Model variant: We'll initially use your fp16 variant; we're interested in int8 if quality holds up.
- Streaming: yes, streaming is required for the customer-facing interactive flow; batch report flow can be non-streaming.

Two asks:
1) Can you include the int8 quantized variant in your A100/H100 comparison?
2) We need a rough cost delta between the H100-based configuration and an A100-based configuration that meets the same SLOs (order of magnitude is OK).

If you can include those items in the validation plan, we can lock a test window next week (Mon/Tue preferred).

Best,

Key constraints: p95 <= 200ms for ~150 tokens (but 20% requests up to 600 tokens), concurrency up to 64 streaming clients, sustained 120 rps, burst to 250 rps. Prefer a 2-3 day wall-clock validation window with parallel runs where feasible.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T14:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity performance validation — next steps

Marissa — proposed plan below. Rafael and I can run the A100/H100 side-by-side; Monica will coordinate test infra and scheduling. High level summary first, then the test matrix.

Executive summary / quick recommendation:
- H100 fp16 yields ~1.6x throughput and ~25-40% lower p95 latency vs A100 fp16 for this model family in our internal runs. Int8 (quant-infer) can further reduce latency and increase throughput but requires quality validation; expect another ~1.2x uplift vs fp16 for some workloads.
- For FinCo's SLOs (p95 <=200ms, 120 rps sustained, 64 concurrent streaming): our estimate is 3 x H100 nodes (reserved) or 6 x A100 nodes to hit targets with a safety buffer for bursts and warm-cache behavior. If FinCo can accept int8 for the interactive path, 2 x H100 could suffice.
- Cost delta (rough): H100 cluster (3 nodes) ~ +30% cost vs A100 cluster (6 nodes) on reserved pricing, but hardware efficiency and lower networking/aggregation overhead typically improves end-to-end user latency and operational simplicity. If int8 is viable, cost of H100 2-node config could be ~parity or slightly cheaper than A100 6-node.

Proposed test matrix (to run in parallel where possible):
1) Baseline validation (both GPUs, fp16):
  - Sequence lengths: 128 / 256 / 512 / 600
  - Concurrency ramps: 1 -> 8 -> 16 -> 32 -> 64 (streaming enabled)
  - Sustained throughput run: 4 hours @ 120 rps (median sequence length ~150 tokens) with 20% heavy requests (600 tokens)
  - Burst window: 10 minutes ramps up to 250 rps to validate headroom/auto-throttle behavior
  - Metrics: p50/p90/p95 latency, time-to-first-byte (streaming), tokens/sec, GPU util, memory footprint, kv-cache hit rates, tail latencies
2) Int8 variant validation (if model supports quant):
  - Same matrix as baseline but focus on quality checks (distributed A/B evals) and perf uplift measurement
3) Cold-start vs warm-cache tests:
  - Cold-start latency measured after full restart and after idle 1 hour
  - Warm-cache run after a 30-minute warmup with realistic traffic replay
4) Stability run: 8-hour soak at 120 rps to capture thermal throttling and memory fragmentation issues

Deliverables:
- Side-by-side benchmark spreadsheet (A100 vs H100 vs int8) - we will share bench results and cost model
- Sizing recommendation with node counts and reserved throughput target
- Short runbook for production warmup and autoscaling/burst guidance

Schedule:
- Prep & infra allocation: 1 business day
- Test runs: 2 business days (parallel runs reduce wall time)
- Analysis and deliverables: 1 business day
If FinCo can provide a preferred test window, we can lock times. Rafael and I recommend Monday/Tuesday next week.
Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
